Profile

What is NAD+?

NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) is a coenzyme in human cells that carries electrons in energy metabolism and is needed by enzymes such as sirtuins and PARPs.12 It is not a peptide.1 NAD+ injections are not FDA-approved, and human data on the effects of IV NAD+ remain limited.34

This page summarizes published sources for information only. It is not medical advice and does not tell anyone to use a product. Questions about your own health belong with a licensed clinician. For questions about an order or a product, contact us.

What sources report

What NAD+ is

NAD+ is short for nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide. PubChem files it under the name nadide (CID 5892, CAS 53-84-9) and lists synonyms that include coenzyme I and diphosphopyridine nucleotide.20215 Its structure is two nucleotides, one carrying nicotinamide and one carrying adenine, joined by a pyrophosphate link.1 Because it contains no amino acids, it is not a peptide and has no peptide sequence.1

What it does in cells

Inside cells, NAD+ accepts electrons and becomes NADH, then hands them on again.1 This redox cycle makes it central to energy metabolism.2 Enzymes that do not move electrons need it too, including sirtuins and PARPs (poly(ADP-ribose) polymerases).2 NAD+ also donates ADP-ribose groups.1 These roles come from laboratory and animal research. They do not by themselves show that extra NAD+ from outside the body improves health.22

Cells make NAD+ by three routes. The de novo route starts from the amino acid tryptophan and runs through the kynurenine pathway. The Preiss-Handler route starts from nicotinic acid in the diet. The salvage route recycles nicotinamide back into NAD+, and the precursors NR and NMN feed into it.2 Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is described as an NAD+ precursor vitamin.23

NAD+ carries an overall negative charge, so it cannot pass through cell membranes on its own.24 Lower NAD+ levels go along with older age in rodents and people, including in skin samples from 49 people aged from newborn to 77. That is a correlation; it does not show that low NAD+ causes aging.225

Human studies of NAD+ injections

Human evidence on NAD+ injections comes from a few small studies. A 2019 pilot gave 8 healthy men one 750 mg IV infusion over 6 hours. There were no adverse events, and plasma NAD+ did not rise for at least the first 2 hours; it was 398% above baseline only at the 6 hour mark.24 A 2026 review of clinic records found that all 6 clients given 500 mg by IV on 4 consecutive days reported moderate to severe symptoms during infusion.4 A 2026 preprint, not yet peer reviewed, tested 100 mg given three ways (IV push, intramuscular, subcutaneous) in groups of 4 to 6 adults.26 These were blood-level and tolerability studies. The authors of the 2026 clinic review state that human data on the efficacy and health effects of IV NAD+ remain limited.4

Benefits people look for

No controlled human trial in these sources shows that NAD+ injections improve energy, memory or aging.4 Most human data on raising NAD+ come from oral precursors. Oral NR raised NAD+ levels or metabolism in trials of 6 and 8 weeks.2314 Even so, a 2023 review found it has shown few clinically relevant effects.27 Each goal, with its evidence level, is covered in NAD+ benefits and uses.

Side effects

In a 2026 review of clinic records, every one of the 6 clients who received 500 mg of NAD+ by IV reported moderate to severe symptoms during the drip. They included abdominal cramping, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, a raised heart rate and chest pressure, and they ended when the drip stopped.4 A slower 6 hour infusion of 750 mg caused no adverse events in 8 men.24 FDA has also received adverse event reports of severe chills, shaking, vomiting and fatigue after NAD+ injectable drugs, which it says are consistent with excessive endotoxin levels.28 Full list: NAD+ side effects.

Dosage information

There is no established or approved human dose for NAD+ injection in the US.3 FDA also found too little clinical data to judge NAD's safety in compounded products.16 The studies on record used 750 mg in one 6 hour IV infusion, 500 mg by IV on each of 4 days, or 100 mg per injection.24426 These amounts describe research, not doses for people. Full details: NAD+ dosage.

Reconstitution and storage

According to FDA, NAD breaks down substantially at room temperature and with light, moisture or alkaline pH.16 The vial sold here contains freeze-dried NAD+ that must be dissolved before lab work; one registered study prepared 100 mg in 2 mL of bacteriostatic water.29 Steps, supplies and concentration math: How to reconstitute NAD+. The research vial and its matching supplies are listed under NAD+ for sale.

Regulatory status

United States

NAD+ is not an FDA-approved drug. On FDA's 503B list, ingredients of approved drugs carry two asterisks, and beta-nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide has none.3 Compounded drugs, including compounded NAD+, are not FDA-approved.12

  • 503A (pharmacies and physicians). On the list updated May 14, 2026, NAD is in Category 1, "Bulk Drug Substances Under Evaluation", together with NADH. It is not in Category 2, the group FDA says raises significant safety risks.6 For Category 1 substances, FDA does not intend to act against licensed compounders who meet its guidance conditions. That holds until a final rule settles the substance's status.3011 Compounding under section 503A also requires a valid patient-specific prescription.12
  • History. FDA evaluated NAD for fatigue in multiple sclerosis. Its Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee voted on May 8, 2017 not to add NAD to the 503A bulks list. FDA's September 5, 2019 proposed rule would not have added it either.16 FDA said it found no published studies supporting that use.16 NAD was still in Category 1 in May 2026, in line with FDA's practice of keeping a substance there until a final rule addresses it.611
  • A related salt. Beta-nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide disodium salt trihydrate is in 503A Category 3, "Nominated Without Adequate Support".6
  • 503B (outsourcing facilities). Beta-nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide is in 503B Category 1 on the list updated March 21, 2025.3 FDA's January 20, 2026 warning letter to the outsourcing facility GenoGenix said NAD+ does not appear on the 503B bulks list. As a result, that firm's NAD+ products did not qualify for 503B exemptions.19

Safety actions

In an October 2024 notice, FDA said compounders were using food-grade NAD+ from repackagers to make IV products.28 In the GenoGenix case, an unopened vial from a lot linked to three emergency room referrals contained 3,360 EU/mL of bacterial endotoxins.19 The related recall of NAD+ for Injection was classified Class I on October 21, 2025.31 As of October 2026, FDA's enforcement database lists 14 recalls of NAD or NADH products classified from 2017 to 2025, most for lack of sterility assurance.32

A "research use only" label does not settle a product's status either. In February 2025, FDA sent a warning letter to a different online peptide seller about semaglutide and tirzepatide. It said such labels did not change its finding that the products were drugs intended for human use, based on the website.33

Outside the US and in sport

A 2026 trial protocol from Beijing Children's Hospital describes injectable Coenzyme I (NAD+) as a marketed product in China (approval number H41024721). It is supplied in 5 mg vials, and its package insert lists coronary heart disease and myocarditis.34 For athletes, the WADA list in force from January 1, 2026 caps IV infusions or injections at 100 mL per 12 hours. The cap applies whatever the drip contains; hospital treatment, surgery and clinical diagnostic investigations are exempt.7

Frequently asked questions

Is NAD like Ozempic?

No. Ozempic (semaglutide) is an FDA-approved GLP-1 receptor agonist used with diet and exercise to improve blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes.8 NAD+ is a coenzyme, not a GLP-1 drug, and has no FDA approval.13 Oral NAD+ precursor trials did not show weight loss: ten weeks of NMN left body weight and fat unchanged in 25 women with prediabetes,9 and twelve weeks of NR had no effect on body composition in 40 obese men.10 More on the brand: What is Ozempic?

Can you get NAD shots?

Not as an approved product in the US. NAD is in FDA's 503A Category 1.6 FDA does not intend to act against licensed pharmacies or physicians compounding with Category 1 substances when its conditions are met.11 Compounding under section 503A needs a valid patient-specific prescription, and compounded drugs are not FDA-approved.12 Even so, the authors of a 2026 clinic study note that IV NAD+ has become widely available in commercial clinics.4

Is NAD just vitamin B3?

No, but the two are linked. Cells turn vitamin precursors such as nicotinic acid and nicotinamide riboside into NAD+, recycle nicotinamide into it, and can also build it from the amino acid tryptophan.2 A dietary lack of niacin causes the disease pellagra, with low NAD+ levels.2 In 2016, FDA had no questions about nicotinamide riboside chloride as a source of vitamin B3 in foods.13 NAD+ itself is the finished coenzyme.

What is an NAD supplement?

The oral trials reviewed here tested NAD+ precursors rather than NAD+ itself: nicotinamide riboside (NR) and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN). In an 8-week trial of 140 adults, oral NR raised whole-blood NAD+ in step with the amount taken.14 Oral NMN raised blood NAD over 60 days in 80 adults.15 FDA noted that nonclinical data suggest NADH, the reduced form, is unstable in acid and likely broken down before absorption when swallowed.16

What are the differences between MOTS-c and NAD+?

MOTS-c is a 16 amino acid peptide encoded in mitochondrial DNA.17 In mice, it prevented insulin resistance linked to age and to a high-fat diet.17 NAD+ is not a peptide at all. It is a dinucleotide coenzyme that carries electrons in energy metabolism and supports enzymes such as sirtuins.12 For the peptide's own evidence, see What is MOTS-c?

Is 5-Amino-1MQ the same as NAD?

No. 5-Amino-1MQ (5-amino-1-methylquinolinium) is, as its name shows, an amine-substituted methylquinolinium. Compounds of that type block the enzyme NNMT, and a potent one was tested in mice with diet-induced obesity.18 NAD+ is a coenzyme. FDA's January 2026 warning letter to the outsourcing facility GenoGenix named the two as separate substances, neither on the 503B bulks list.19
